comparison: Both evaluate initial clustering and cell population identification (C1, C21-C26). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of methodology and quantitative support, while peer reviewers praised the approach as 'exceptionally rigorous' and 'technically strong.' Both find the work SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates rod maturation states (C27-C31) as SUPPORTED with specific attention to gene expression patterns and ontology enrichments. Peer R1 groups these claims with broader clustering results and praises the overall analysis without specific concerns.

OpenEval evaluates cone subtype identification (C32-C35) as SUPPORTED, noting novel S-cone markers and validation of known markers. Peer R1 includes some of these claims (C32, C34, C35) in their broad endorsement of cell population identification.

OpenEval rates L/M cone maturation states (C36-C40) as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (5 cells), while peer R1 includes these claims in their SUPPORTED evaluation without raising concerns about statistical power.

Both evaluate external validation with independent datasets (C41-C42). OpenEval emphasizes methodological consistency strengthening confidence, while peer R15 groups this with other contextual literature citations as appropriately positioned work.

Both evaluate SCENIC regulon analysis (C43-C49) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of statistical support and biological consistency, while peer reviewers explicitly praised regulon analyses as providing 'insight into key transcription factor programs.'

OpenEval evaluates unexpected RNA co-expression patterns (C50-C55) as SUPPORTED, noting modest fold-changes suggest post-transcriptional regulation. Peer R3 groups this with broader isoform findings and strongly endorses the discovery as 'crucial' and 'only really possible with full length scRNAseq.'

Both evaluate novel NRL isoforms (C56-C62) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple validation methods, while peer reviewers called the discovery of 'distinct active vs inactive mRNA isoforms' crucial for understanding cell fate decisions.

Both evaluate long-read validation of NRL isoforms (C63-C68) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes with statistical support (p<0.0001), while peer R3 endorses this as part of the broader isoform discovery praised as novel and important.

Both evaluate Tr-NRL protein and function (C69-C73) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes lack of protein detection suggests post-transcriptional regulation but functional assay demonstrates suppressive capability. Peer R3 acknowledges this finding without criticism as part of endorsed isoform work.

Both evaluate THRB isoform regulation (C74-C82) as SUPPORTED with perfect claim overlap. OpenEval emphasizes statistical support and convergence of multiple validation methods, while peer reviewers found the 'model of cell type-dependent splicing for NRL and THRB particularly intriguing.'

Both evaluate RXRG findings (C83-C85) as SUPPORTED with perfect claim overlap. OpenEval notes this negative result distinguishes RXRG from NRL/THRB regulation, while peer R5 acknowledges this as part of comprehensive isoform analysis without specific discussion.

Both evaluate high-resolution clustering of precursors (C86-C92) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes validation through marker genes and ontology enrichment, while peer R6 praises identification of precursor populations and notes the finding 'clarifies a long-standing notion in the field.'

Both evaluate immediately post-mitotic precursors (C93-C102) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges limited statistical power but notes consistent trends, while peer R6 explicitly praises the identification of these populations and their characterization.

Both evaluate external validation of early precursors (C103-C108) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with independent dataset supports biological validity, while peer R6 acknowledges cross-validation strengthened findings without raising concerns.

Both evaluate regulon dynamics during RPC-to-photoreceptor transition (C109-C114) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical support (p<0.05) and mechanistic insights, while peer R6 groups this with broader precursor characterization they praised.

Both evaluate 'bridge region' findings (C115-C120) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergence of regulon analysis and RNA FISH validation showing cone-directed cells, while peer R7 states the insight into mixed transcripts 'is important and clarifies a long-standing notion.'

Both evaluate temporal resolution of marker co-expression (C121-C125) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes sequential appearance and spatial separation in UMAP, while peer R7 endorses the finding that co-expression occurs after fate determination.

Both evaluate iCP marker characterization (C126-C136) as SUPPORTED with high claim overlap. OpenEval notes validation in independent dataset and spatial validation with statistical support, while peer R8 explicitly mentions 'New markers of subpopulations are also uncovered, such as CHRNA1.'

Both evaluate OLIG2/LHX9 regulon activity (C137-C138) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes discordance between regulon activity and RNA expression suggests post-transcriptional regulation, while peer R8 groups this with broader marker characterization they endorsed.

Both evaluate L/M cone maturation as continuum (C139-C141) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes sequential gene expression and lack of distinct regulon differences, while peer R9 praises the 'gradient of lncRNAs in maturing cones' as novel.

Both evaluate sequential lncRNA expression (C142-C145) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergence of pseudotime and RNA FISH validation, while peer R9 explicitly states the 'gradient of lncRNAs in maturing cones is novel' and 'opens up a new line of questioning.'

Both evaluate MYCN as cone-enriched factor (C146-C150) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergence of differential expression, protein validation, and regulon analysis, while peer R10 states 'the potential involvement of the SYK and MYC pathways with RB...aligns with previous literature.'

Both evaluate SYK expression dynamics (C151-C154) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes stage-specific expression with RNA and protein validation, while peer R11 acknowledges 'The finding that SYK mRNA is naturally expressed in cone precursors is novel.'

OpenEval rates SYK functional evidence (C155-C156) as SUPPORTED but notes need for genetic validation. Peer R11 rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'Validation of the SYK inhibitor data e.g. by genetic means, is not included' and noting this caveat limits mechanistic certainty.

Both evaluate methodological advantages and NRL findings (C157-C161) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multiple validation approaches strengthen conclusions, while peer R12 praises full-length scRNA-seq as enabling these discoveries.

Both evaluate THRB regulation mechanisms (C162-C165) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes novel PTT findings and methodological cautions about 3' end-counting, while peer R13 finds the 'model of cell type-dependent splicing for NRL and THRB particularly intriguing.'

Both evaluate cell state characterization summary (C166-C169) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes internal consistency and mechanistic context from prior knowledge, while peer R12 groups this with broader methodological praise.

Both evaluate lncRNA expression dynamics summary (C170-C172) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes validation in prior studies and spatial validation, while peer R12 acknowledges this as part of the comprehensive analysis they endorsed.

Both evaluate identification of immature precursors and developmental model (C173-C178) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes characterization is well-supported and model is reasonable synthesis, while peer R12 praises the methodological advantages enabling these findings.

Both evaluate temporal dynamics of cross-lineage markers (C179-C181) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of independent dataset and spatial validation, while peer R14 endorses the interpretation that co-expression occurs after fate determination.

Both evaluate reinterpretation of retinoblastoma patterns (C182-C183) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes sound logic that normal cone precursors express rod markers, while peer R14 acknowledges this resolves prior uncertainties about mixed gene expression.

Both evaluate early precursor marker characterization (C184-C187) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes well-documented expression patterns with reasonable inferences about OLIG2 role, while peer R14 groups this with broader findings that clarify developmental processes.

Both evaluate MYCN connection to retinoblastoma (C188-C189) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes well-supported expression data but inference relies on prior work, while peer R10 states the MYC pathway involvement 'aligns with previous literature, offering additional insights.'

OpenEval evaluates SYK as cone precursor-specific factor (C190-C192) as SUPPORTED but notes need for genetic validation. Peer R11 rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of genetic validation leaves mechanistic role uncertain despite novel expression finding.
